"We need smarter cities, not “smart cities”.

Technology can play a key role in improving #energy efficiency and access in cities. From smart meters to AI-enabled grid management. These are very familiar examples of “smart cities”. But cities are more than 5G and Big Data. They are drivers of opportunity, prosperity, and progress, generating 80% of global GDP. By 2050, 68% of the world’s population will live in cities, placing them on the front lines of climate change.

A focus on building “#SmartCities” risks turning cities into technology projects. We talk about “users” instead of people. And there can be a focus on discrete deployments of technology rather than the ‘connective tissue’ which makes cities the kinds of places where people want to live, work, and play. This risks constraining inclusive and sustainable urban development.

Truly smart cities recognize the ambiguity of lives and livelihoods. They use a broader innovation toolkit, where technology supports real needs, including energy systems, rather than defining the city itself.

Discover why truly smart cities are defined by people and connection, not just the deployment of technology, and what this means for energy innovation in cities.

Learn more : https://lnkd.in/ghZnHY7g

#EnergyForDevelopment"
MIT Technology Review
